title: Sandwiching polynomials fool independent distributions
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. Suppose there are degree-at-most-$k$ polynomials $P_\ell,P_u$, expressed as linear combinations of the monomials $x\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ for subsets $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, such that $P_\ell(x)\le f(x)\le P_u(x)$ for every $x$, and the uniform average of $P_u-P_\ell$ is at most $\varepsilon$. For every probability distribution $\mu$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ whose marginal on each set of at most $k$ coordinates is uniform, the absolute difference between the expectations of $f$ under $\mu$ and under the uniform distribution is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of lower and upper degree-at-most-$k$ polynomials bounding $f$ pointwise
Uniform average of the upper polynomial minus the lower polynomial is at most $\varepsilon$
Every marginal on at most $k$ coordinates is uniform
